compression.title: Database Compression
compression.desc: Migrate historical request bodies from plaintext into a deduplicated compressed form. Each run rewrites one batch and can be paused; an interrupted run resumes from its watermark.
compression.original_hint: Total original bytes across the table, measured once when a run starts
compression.original_unmeasured: Not measured yet: one "Start migration" measures it (reads record headers only, changes nothing)
compression.stored_hint: Body column + chunk groups + block index (index ≈ {{block}}, an estimate)
compression.ratio_running: Migration in progress: this climbs as rows change form (starts near 1.0×)
compression.reclaimable_hint_off: Freed but still inside the file. With auto_vacuum=0 the file only grows; VACUUM is required to return this to disk.
compression.reclaimable_hint_on: Freed and returnable to disk via incremental vacuum.
compression.rows_hint: Told apart by whether the column holds plaintext or a frame
compression.blocks_hint: Groups total {{size}} on disk; each block row is shared by several bodies
compression.db_unavailable: Database stats unavailable (the migration is writing and this read hit the lock) — it retries automatically, no refresh needed
compression.db_unavailable_short: Database stats are temporarily unavailable; they refresh automatically
compression.db_stale: Database stats measured at {{time}} (too busy to measure right now)

reclaim.label: Reclaim:
reclaim.cost: Reclaim holds the write lock throughout: writes queue and fail after 5s. Reads are unaffected. Each round stops at 90s; the rest goes next time.
reclaim.title: Reclaim free pages
reclaim.desc: Return freelist pages to the filesystem. It does not touch data — repeatable, interruptible, nothing lost.
reclaim.warn: While it runs, log writes and other writes queue and fail after busy_timeout (5s); reads are unaffected.

reason.budget: time budget reached; the rest goes next round
reason.no_auto_vacuum: this database has auto_vacuum off, so reclaim is a no-op
reason.stalled: a batch freed nothing and the freelist did not shrink, so it stopped early (see the error below)
reason.insufficient_space: not enough disk, skipped (service started anyway)

blocked.busy_migration: A migration is running; reclaim must wait — they share one maintenance lock.
blocked.no_stats: The database cannot be measured right now, so there is no way to tell whether there is anything to free.
blocked.no_auto_vacuum: This database has auto_vacuum=0, so incremental reclaim is a no-op here (0s, file shrinks by nothing). Shrinking it needs a full VACUUM; or start once with DB_AUTO_VACUUM_REBUILD=on to convert it to INCREMENTAL.
blocked.nothing: Nothing to reclaim — the file has no holes left.

backup.label: Backup probe:
backup.stale: The backup found is smaller than the database — likely pre-migration, so restoring it would lose data
backup.forced: Run without a backup after operator confirmation

compression.policy_disabled: Automatic progress: off (manual runs still work)
compression.no_backup_desc: Migration rewrites the storage form of historical request bodies in place. The easiest recovery path is restoring a backup — which requires that one actually exists.
compression.no_backup_hint: Copying the database file first and then returning here is the safer route. If you continue, this run is recorded as having had no backup.
compression.rollback_desc: Restore every compressed request body back to plaintext. This rewrites the whole database.
compression.rollback_warn: Reverting makes the database substantially larger (measured: 1.46 GiB → 7.05 GiB) and discards every gain from migration — a full re-run is needed to get it back. Make sure a usable backup exists first.
compression.edit_desc: These govern how large a batch is, not how hard the data is compressed. Chunk and group sizes are fixed in code — changing them would make already-stored data unreadable.
compression.policy_switch_hint: When on, the service periodically continues unfinished migration. Manual runs are unaffected by this switch.
compression.batch_rows_hint: 1–4096; out-of-range values are clamped. Larger batches pack groups fuller but hold more raw text in memory at once.
compression.batch_bytes_hint: Byte cap; a batch always keeps at least one row.
compression.batch_interval_hint: 0–5000; out-of-range values are clamped. This tunes how much of the time the migration holds the database, not how fast it is: larger means an idler database and a longer migration.
compression.quiesce_hint: Rows written more recently than this are left alone, so half-written records are never migrated.

toast.paused: Pause requested; the current batch will finish first
